entries.summary: Delete a Deployment and its managed ReplicaSets and Pods.

cases.when: manifests are in git and the workload has no persistent volume
cases.inverse: kubectl apply -f captured manifest
cases.note: the replacement has new UIDs and a gap in service history
the spec can often be recreated but the live rollout state and terminated Pods are gone

entries.summary: Scale a Deployment down to fewer replicas.

cases.when: the prior replica count was captured and replicas were greater than zero
cases.inverse: kubectl scale deployment to the captured replica count
cases.window: until another actor changes the scale target
cases.note: the Deployment object remains the same and the inverse only restores desired count
Pods killed during the scale down cannot be brought back with the same identity

cases.when: the Secret manifest or sealed source is in git
cases.inverse: kubectl apply -f captured Secret manifest
cases.window: while the secret material remains valid
cases.note: the recreated Secret gets a new resource version and consumers may have observed an outage
without a captured value the secret bytes are no longer recoverable from the API

entries.summary: Delete a Namespace and cascade deletion to namespaced resources.

cases.inverse: kubectl create namespace with captured labels and annotations
cases.note: the namespace object can be recreated but its UID changes

cases.when: manifests are in git and every persistent volume uses Retain
cases.inverse: reapply manifests and rebind retained volumes
cases.window: while retained volumes and images exist
cases.note: the control plane objects can be rebuilt but workload identity and event history change
cascade deletion can remove workloads, claims and controller state with no exact inverse

cases.when: the bound PersistentVolume reclaim policy is Retain
cases.inverse: recreate the claim and bind it to the retained volume
cases.note: the data may remain but claim identity and consumers must be repaired
a Delete reclaim policy can destroy the backing volume with the claim

cases.when: chart values were captured and every persistent volume uses Retain
cases.inverse: helm install with captured chart and values, then rebind retained volumes
cases.window: while chart artifacts and retained volumes exist
cases.note: Helm can recreate objects but cannot preserve UIDs or downtime-free state
hooks and cascading resource deletion can remove state that Helm history cannot restore

entries.summary: Delete a ConfigMap used by workloads.

cases.when: the ConfigMap manifest is in git
cases.inverse: kubectl apply -f captured ConfigMap manifest
cases.window: while the referenced data stays current
cases.note: workloads may have restarted or failed during the absence
the previous key values are not recoverable without a captured manifest

entries.summary: Delete a Service and its cluster virtual IP.

cases.when: the Service manifest is in git
cases.inverse: kubectl apply -f captured Service manifest
cases.note: the recreated Service can receive a different cluster IP unless it was pinned
clients may have cached or observed the missing endpoint even after recreation

entries.summary: Apply a Terraform plan that may destroy or replace resources.

cases.when: the plan has zero destroy actions
cases.inverse: terraform apply the captured rollback plan
cases.window: while providers keep prior remote state
cases.note: remote provider side effects can still leave traces outside state

cases.when: destroy actions exist and every destroyed resource is stateless and re-creatable from configuration
cases.inverse: terraform apply the prior configuration
cases.window: while provider names and quotas remain available
cases.note: the resource graph can be rebuilt but identities and outage history change
destroying stateful resources can remove provider-side data with no exact inverse

entries.summary: Remove an address from Terraform state.

cases.inverse: restore the captured state backup
cases.window: until another apply depends on the modified state
cases.note: restoring state is exact for Terraform but may conflict with later remote changes
the remote object may survive but Terraform forgets ownership and future applies can drift

entries.summary: Force unlock a Terraform state lock.

cases.when: the recorded lock holder is inactive
cases.inverse: no inverse needed
cases.note: removing a stale lock only returns the backend to the usable state
unlocking an active writer can allow concurrent applies and corrupt state ordering

cases.when: the workspace state backup exists and no resources remain
cases.inverse: recreate workspace and restore the captured state
cases.window: while backend history retains the backup
cases.note: the workspace name can return but backend audit history records the deletion
deleting a workspace can discard the last copy of state for live resources

cases.when: the prior variable set was captured
cases.inverse: recreate variables from the captured set
cases.note: secret variables cannot be read back after deletion unless intercepted before the call
write-only secret values are lost when no capture exists

entries.summary: Transfer a public repository to another owner.

cases.when: the repository is public and the target owner will transfer it back
cases.inverse: request transfer back to the original owner
cases.note: public clones and forks made during the transfer cannot be recalled
ownership and access may be lost without a unilateral inverse

entries.summary: Remove a member from a GitHub organization.

cases.when: membership, teams and roles were captured
cases.inverse: reinvite the member and restore captured teams and roles
cases.window: while the user accepts the invitation
cases.note: the access gap and audit log remain even if permissions return
access can be re-granted but private forks, tokens and automation may be disrupted

cases.when: the secret values are captured in the operator vault
cases.inverse: gh secret set for each captured secret
cases.window: while the secret values remain valid
cases.note: GitHub cannot reveal deleted secret values, so only an external capture makes this reversible
write-only secret values are gone from GitHub after deletion

cases.when: overwritten commits remain reachable and the default branch does not deploy
cases.inverse: force push the captured prior tip
cases.note: restoring history can invalidate work based on the new tip
lost commits or triggered deployments cannot be exactly undone

cases.when: the prior protection rule was captured
cases.inverse: recreate the captured branch protection rule
cases.note: writes accepted while protection was absent remain in history
the rule can be rebuilt but unreviewed pushes during the gap remain

cases.when: team membership and repository grants were captured
cases.inverse: recreate the team and restore captured grants
cases.window: while members and repositories still exist
cases.note: the team slug and audit trail can change
permissions can be reassembled but exact team identity and audit continuity are lost

cases.when: the public key and write access flag were captured
cases.inverse: recreate the deploy key from the captured public key
cases.window: while the private key still exists wherever it was generated
cases.note: GitHub stores only the public key, so runtime reachability depends on the external private key
a new key can restore access but every consumer must rotate

entries.summary: Change a private repository to public.

cases.when: the repository has no private data and the visibility change has not propagated to mirrors
cases.inverse: set repository visibility back to private
cases.note: the setting can be restored but the exposure event is still visible in audit history
making code public cannot unshare clones or cached copies

cases.when: the environment secret values are captured in the operator vault
cases.inverse: gh secret set with the captured environment scope
cases.note: the environment protection rules do not store secret plaintext
write-only environment secret values are gone after deletion

cases.when: the project is inside the restore window
cases.inverse: restore the project from GitLab pending deletion
cases.note: webhooks and runners may need repair after restore
after permanent deletion the repository, issues and packages are gone from GitLab

cases.when: overwritten commits remain reachable and the branch does not deploy
cases.inverse: force push the captured prior tip
cases.note: pipelines and reviews created from the new tip remain as traces
lost commits or triggered deployments cannot be exactly undone

entries.summary: Remove a member from a GitLab group.

cases.when: group roles and project memberships were captured
cases.inverse: reinvite the member and restore captured roles
cases.window: while the user accepts the invitation
cases.note: the access gap and audit event remain
access can be restored but tokens and running jobs may already have failed

cases.when: the variable values were captured in the operator vault
cases.inverse: recreate the CI variables from the captured values
cases.note: masked variables are write-only in GitLab after creation
deleted masked variable values cannot be read back from GitLab

entries.summary: Transfer a project into a public namespace.

cases.when: the namespace owner will transfer it back and the project has no private data
cases.inverse: request transfer back to the original namespace
cases.note: public fetches during the transfer cannot be recalled
project ownership can be lost without a unilateral restore path

entries.summary: Delete a GitLab protected branch rule.

cases.when: the protected branch rule was captured
cases.inverse: recreate the protected branch rule
cases.note: pushes accepted while protection was absent remain in history
the rule can be rebuilt but the protection gap cannot be erased

cases.inverse: restore the repository from the captured backup
cases.note: repository ids, hooks and issue side effects may differ after restore
without a backup the repository database rows and git data are removed

cases.inverse: force push the captured prior tip
cases.note: restoring the tip changes history again for anyone who pulled the new one
unreachable commits may be garbage collected with no service restore path

entries.summary: Remove a member from a Gitea organization.

cases.when: team memberships and repository grants were captured
cases.inverse: reinvite the member and restore captured teams
cases.note: access continuity and audit history are not erased
permissions can be reconstructed but work depending on the access may already have failed

cases.when: the secret values are captured in the operator vault
cases.inverse: recreate the captured secrets
cases.note: secret plaintext is not readable after creation
deleted write-only secret values cannot be recovered from Gitea

entries.summary: Transfer a repository to a public owner.

cases.when: the target owner will transfer it back and the repository has no private data
cases.inverse: request transfer back to the original owner
cases.note: public clones during the transfer cannot be recalled
ownership may be lost with no unilateral inverse

cases.when: the full project payload was captured
cases.inverse: recreate the project from the captured payload
cases.window: while teams and issue ids are still meaningful
cases.note: Linear can recreate content but not preserve every id or notification trace
exports can mitigate loss but project identity and history are not exactly restorable

cases.inverse: recreate each issue from the captured payload
cases.window: while referenced projects and teams exist
cases.note: issue identifiers and notification history change
deleted issue descriptions and comments are not recoverable without capture

cases.when: team settings, members and workflow states were captured
cases.inverse: recreate the team and restore captured settings
cases.note: the team key and issue links may change
work can be reorganized but team identity and routing history are gone

entries.summary: Scrub personal data from Linear workspace records.

cases.when: the scrub only redacts data already exported to the compliance archive
cases.inverse: restore operational references from the archive where allowed
cases.note: privacy erasure can be mitigated for operations but should not be reversed into the product
a completed privacy scrub is intentionally destructive

cases.when: the project remains restorable from archive
cases.inverse: unarchive the project
cases.window: while the archive state is retained
cases.note: automation that skipped archived projects may already have run
the project can be recreated but scheduling and notification side effects remain

cases.when: the project is inside Jira trash and project data is retained
cases.inverse: restore the project from trash
cases.note: project restoration leaves deletion and restoration audit events
permanent project deletion removes issues, configuration and history

cases.when: the interceptor captured issues, comments and attachments
cases.inverse: recreate issues from the captured payload
cases.window: while referenced projects and users exist
cases.note: issue keys and notifications cannot be exactly preserved
bulk deleted issue content is not recoverable without capture

entries.summary: Scrub a user's personal data from Jira.

cases.when: the scrub is limited to reversible display name masking
cases.inverse: restore display names where policy allows
cases.note: privacy actions are policy constrained and audit-visible
completed erasure of user personal data is intentionally irreversible

cases.when: the workflow XML and scheme bindings were captured
cases.inverse: import the workflow and restore captured scheme bindings
cases.note: issues moved during the gap may stay on different paths
workflow shape can be rebuilt but transition history and automation gaps remain

cases.when: the board filter and settings were captured
cases.inverse: recreate the board from captured settings
cases.note: board id and sprint side effects may change
reports and filters can be rebuilt but board identity and analytics history change

cases.when: the project is inside the restore window
cases.inverse: restore the project from Asana deleted projects
cases.note: notifications and integrations may have observed the deletion
after the restore window expires project data is permanently deleted

cases.inverse: recreate tasks from captured payloads
cases.note: task ids, activity history and notifications cannot be exactly preserved
deleted task bodies and comments are not recoverable without capture

cases.when: team members, projects and settings were captured
cases.inverse: recreate the team and restore captured membership
cases.note: team identity and audit history change
membership can be rebuilt but access gaps and integration failures remain

cases.when: portfolio membership and fields were captured
cases.inverse: recreate the portfolio from captured settings
cases.note: portfolio id and reporting continuity change
the visible grouping can be rebuilt but historical reporting continuity is lost

entries.summary: Remove a member from an Asana workspace.

cases.when: member access and team memberships were captured
cases.inverse: reinvite the member and restore captured access
cases.window: while the user accepts the invitation
cases.note: tasks reassigned or automation triggered during the gap remain changed
permissions can be restored but access-dependent work may already have failed

cases.when: project settings and DSNs were captured and events were exported
cases.inverse: recreate the project and import supported settings
cases.note: event ids, issue grouping and inbound DSNs do not return exactly
deleting the project removes issue and event history from Sentry

cases.inverse: recreate tracking from exported events where supported
cases.note: Sentry issue grouping and comments cannot be exactly replayed
deleted issues and events are not restorable from the service

entries.summary: Remove a member from a Sentry organization.

cases.when: member role and team assignments were captured
cases.inverse: reinvite the member and restore captured assignments
cases.window: while the user accepts the invitation
cases.note: the access gap and audit event remain
access can be restored but alerts and ownership workflows may already have changed

cases.when: applications can receive a newly issued DSN through the deploy pipeline
cases.inverse: create a new DSN and deploy it to clients
cases.note: the old DSN cannot be unrevoked, so clients must rotate
revoked ingestion credentials can strand clients that cannot be updated

cases.when: the scrub removes only replay data already exported to an allowed archive
cases.inverse: use the archive for investigation where policy allows
cases.note: privacy scrubbing should not be reversed into Sentry
completed replay scrubbing destroys diagnostic data

cases.when: point in time recovery covers the table
cases.inverse: restore to a new database and copy the table back
cases.note: restore is table-scoped only after manual copy and leaves audit traces
truncate removes rows without row-level undo information

cases.when: point in time recovery covers the database
cases.inverse: restore to a new database and copy schema and data back
cases.note: dependent policies, grants and generated ids need reconciliation
dropping the table removes schema and data with no service-side undelete

entries.summary: Purge every object in a Supabase Storage bucket.

cases.when: all objects were mirrored before the purge
cases.inverse: upload mirrored objects back into the bucket
cases.note: object metadata and signed URL observations may differ
purged objects are deleted from storage with no version restore path

cases.inverse: none needed
cases.note: a no-op bulk delete changes no account state

cases.when: user exports and provider identities were captured
cases.inverse: recreate users where policy and providers allow
cases.window: while exports and external identities remain valid
cases.note: password hashes, sessions and auth UIDs cannot be exactly restored
deleted auth users, sessions and credentials have no exact inverse

cases.when: the function source and secrets manifest are in git
cases.inverse: redeploy the function from git
cases.note: deploy history and endpoint downtime remain as traces
without source control the deployed code cannot be recovered from deletion

entries.summary: Delete a Supabase row level security policy.

cases.inverse: recreate the policy from captured SQL
cases.note: rows read or written while the policy was absent are not undone
the policy can be rebuilt but exposure or denied work during the gap remains

cases.when: the branch has no unique data
cases.inverse: recreate the branch from its parent
cases.note: branch identity and logs change but data loss is absent
unique branch data is gone when the branch is deleted

cases.when: the secret values are captured in the operator vault
cases.inverse: set each secret from the captured values
cases.note: secret plaintext is write-only after storage
deleted secret values cannot be read back from Supabase

cases.when: the full product payloads were captured
cases.inverse: recreate products from captured payloads
cases.window: while media and variant references remain available
cases.note: product ids, URLs and app side effects can change
deleted product data and media links are not recoverable without capture

entries.summary: Publish a theme over the live Shopify theme.

cases.when: the previous live theme id was captured
cases.inverse: publish the captured previous theme
cases.window: while the previous theme is retained
cases.note: publishing switches the live pointer and does not delete the old theme
customers may see or cache the new live theme before rollback

entries.summary: Cancel many Shopify orders at once.

cases.when: no fulfilment or payment capture exists for the orders
cases.inverse: recreate draft orders from captured payloads
cases.note: order numbers and notifications change
refunds and restocking can mitigate harm but the cancellations cannot be erased

entries.summary: Erase customer personal data from Shopify.

cases.inverse: cancel the pending erasure request
cases.note: after processing, privacy erasure is meant to be permanent
completed customer data erasure is intentionally irreversible

cases.inverse: recreate discounts from captured definitions
cases.note: redemption analytics and app side effects are not exactly restored
discounts can be recreated but campaigns and customer behavior during the gap remain changed

cases.when: the number is still inside Twilio's reclaim window
cases.inverse: attempt to reclaim the released number
cases.window: while the provider holds the number
cases.note: provider-side release is not a guaranteed inverse and inbound messages during the gap are lost
the number can be assigned to another customer and cannot be recovered

cases.inverse: recreate the service and attach available senders
cases.note: service SID, delivery history and inbound routing identity change
sender routing and service identity are lost without a captured configuration

entries.summary: Delete a Twilio domain or branded link domain.

cases.when: DNS records and provider configuration were captured
cases.inverse: recreate the domain configuration and DNS records
cases.window: while the domain remains under operator control
cases.note: provider verification and reputation history may not return exactly
a deleted provider domain can lose verification and reputation state

cases.when: all clients can rotate to a new key
cases.inverse: create a new key and deploy it to clients
cases.note: the revoked key cannot be unrevoked, so rotation is mitigation only
unreachable clients that only know the revoked key lose access permanently

entries.summary: Delete a SendGrid authenticated sending domain.

cases.when: DNS records and domain settings were captured
cases.inverse: recreate the domain and DNS records
cases.note: sender reputation and verification continuity can still be damaged
deleting a sending domain can break authentication and reputation with no exact inverse

cases.when: all clients can rotate to a new key
cases.inverse: create a new API key and deploy it to clients
cases.note: the old key cannot be restored after revocation
unreachable senders that only know the revoked key lose mail capability

cases.inverse: restore suppressions from the captured list
cases.note: messages sent during the gap may have reached suppressed recipients
suppression state can be rebuilt but unwanted sends during the gap remain

cases.inverse: recreate the template and versions from capture
cases.window: while template id references can be updated
cases.note: the template id changes and clients may need redeploy
template content is not recoverable without a captured copy
